head_commit.message:
fix: pipeline timeouts, fence leaks, the generation-application fk, and rust edition 2024 (#996)

* chore: apply cargo fix --edition ahead of the rust 2024 switch

Mechanical prep for the edition bump, still on edition = "2021" so
this is reviewable apart from the flag flip in the next commit:

- gen -> r#gen (extension_bridge/{answer_assist,assist_registry,stream}
  + tests): `gen` becomes a reserved keyword in 2024 (future generators).
- expr -> expr_2021 macro fragment specifier (tests/eval.rs): 2024
  widened what `expr` matches; `expr_2021` keeps the old matcher.
- match-ergonomics closure pattern (commands/autopilot.rs):
  `|(_, &idx)|` -> `|&(_, &idx)|` for a HashMap::iter() closure.
- RPIT capture opt-out (pipeline/resume/mod.rs deadline_guard):
  `+ 'static` -> `+ 'static + use<>` — 2024 auto-captures all in-scope
  lifetimes in `-> impl Trait`; QualityCtx<'a>'s `'a` was never used by
  this closure, so `use<>` restores the old non-capturing signature.
- cargo fmt: r#gen is 2 chars longer than gen, which pushed one line
  in assist_registry.rs over the wrap width.

cargo test --workspace: 3970 passed (matches the pre-migration baseline).

* chore: switch the tauri crate to rust edition 2024

Flips edition = "2021" -> "2024" (rust-version stays at 1.95, well
below the toolchain pin of 1.97.1). Two supporting changes land in the
same commit since neither is meaningful without the flip:

- rustfmt.toml: pin style_edition = "2021" alongside edition = "2024".
  `cargo fmt` passes the crate's Cargo.toml edition to rustfmt, which
  overrides rustfmt.toml's own (now-stale) `edition` key for style
  purposes; without this pin, the edition bump silently reformats
  dozens of untouched files (import sort order, assert! wrapping).
  Verified zero source reformatting with the pin in place.
- src/lib.rs: #![allow(clippy::collapsible_if)], next to the existing
  #![deny(clippy::await_holding_lock)]. Edition 2024 legalizes
  let-chains, so clippy's (default clippy::all, not pedantic)
  collapsible_if lint newly fires at ~96 pre-existing nested
  if/if-let sites across every domain in the crate under
  -D warnings. None of the 96 are defects — this is a style
  modernization deliberately deferred to its own follow-up rather
  than folded into the edition flip (owner decision), not something
  cargo fix --edition touches or can safely bulk-apply.

Per-site review of the two edition-2024 semantic changes that matter here:

- The 10 `if let Ok(guard) = x.{lock,read,write}()` sites in src/ (grep
  found exactly 10): none has an else branch, so the "guard held
  through else in 2021, dropped before else in 2024" temporary-scope
  change cannot apply to any of them — confirmed both by reading each
  site and by the fact that cargo fix --edition's own drop-order
  warnings never named any of these files/lines.
- The 5 `-> impl Trait` sites (grep found exactly 5): 2 are native
  trait-method RPITIT (salary_research, commands/ai), which capture
  all in-scope generics by default regardless of edition since their
  own stabilization; 1 (ats_seed::by_ats) already carries an explicit
  use<'_> bound that overrides the edition default; 1
  (Section::bullets) already necessarily captures its only in-scope
  lifetime via the elided &ParsedLine return; 1
  (QualityCtx::deadline_guard) needed and got + use<> from
  cargo fix --edition to keep 'a out of its 'static-bound closure.

Post-flip verification: cargo check --all-targets --all-features is
warning-free (matches edition-2021 baseline); cargo clippy --all-targets
--all-features --locked -- -D warnings is clean (0 errors — confirms
100% of the pre-allow 96 errors were collapsible_if, no other lint
class hid behind it); cargo test --workspace is 3970 passed, identical
to baseline; cargo doc --no-deps exits 0 with the same 214 pre-existing
rustdoc link warnings as edition 2021 (unrelated to this change).

* docs(rust): record what the edition-2024 deferrals actually cover

Review found three comments that were true but incomplete, each in a place a
future reader has to trust without re-deriving:

- The collapsible_if allow is WIDER than its stated reason. The lint also
  covers plain nested ifs, unrelated to let-chains, so it leaves a small real
  coverage hole -- and it applies to the lib crate root only, so the same code
  in tests/ or benches/ still hard-fails -D warnings.
- The style_edition pin is debt with a price tag: unpinning reformats ~200
  files in 374 hunks, so it needs its own commit rather than riding along.
- expr_2021 reads as a deliberate pin and is a cargo fix artifact; nothing
  here needs the old matcher.

Comments only -- no behavior, no lint change. fmt and clippy re-run clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: anchor the pipeline elapsed timer on the run's own start time

GeneratingPanel reset its elapsed clock to 0:00 on every remount because it
was seeded from a ref set at component-mount time. Navigating away and back
unmounts the whole TailorFlow tree (ApplicationDetailPage only renders it
while the Documents tab is active) and reconnects to the still-running
backend job, so the clock restarted while the run itself hadn't. During the
long, non-streaming Analyze stage that timer is the only liveness signal,
so a reset made a slow-but-healthy run read as stuck.

Anchor on PipelineRunDetail.startedAt instead - a timestamp the backend
already records on pipeline_runs and returns on every run-record fetch, so
it survives a remount for free with no new state to persist. It's a per-run
timestamp, not per-step: the run's own event trail could reconstruct a
per-step start too, but that requires walking a persisted event log across
a step-to-stage fold and can drift for a poll cycle after a live reconnect,
so a simple, always-correct per-run number wins. The caption's copy changes
accordingly (pipeline.step.elapsedTotal, en+de) since it now reads total run
time rather than time-in-this-step.

* fix(pipeline): reject a humanize/repair candidate that echoes its own fence tag

A real run exported a résumé with <humanize_document> as the name and
</humanize_document> as the last line: the model echoed the fence wrapper
humanize_user sent it in, and every existing guard (length floor,
critical/voice-flag comparison) grades content, not shape, so a wrapper
that only ADDS length sailed through clean.

is_usable_rewrite now also rejects any candidate containing a registered
fence tag, checked against the full prompt_fence registry rather than one
hardcoded name, and reverts to the original (never strips-and-keeps) since
a model that echoed one tag may have echoed other scaffolding too.

repair's is_usable_replacement gets the same gate: its prompt wraps the
section under <resume_section> and asks for the replacement back, the
same shape a leak could take.

draft and cover_letter have no shape validation at all (audited, not
fixed here — unlike humanize/repair they are the sole producer for a run
with no "original" to revert to, so a fix needs a fail-open/fail-closed
design decision rather than a one-line gate).

* fix: give a per-call pipeline timeout a stop reason and a message

analyze_job/match_evidence/strategy (and repair/humanize) hit their
non-streaming per-call deadline and the run recorded no reason at all:
StoppedReason::Timeout existed in the enum but had no producer, so a
timed-out run surfaced as "stopped" with nothing further to say.

- Each provider's complete_impl (ollama/openai/anthropic/gemini)
  classifies a reqwest deadline expiry (is_timeout()) as
  AppError::Timeout instead of folding it into the generic
  "unreachable" Network error.
- Pipeline::run_hooked flags that on StageOutcome, and
  RunHooks::after (via the new apply_timeout) records
  StoppedReason::Timeout plus which stage and how long on the run
  ledger.
- execute replaces the propagated error with an actionable message
  (stage + duration, content-free per ADR-027) before it reaches
  job_fail, so the existing raw-error banner has something to show.
- The renderer's STOPPED_SUFFIX map and both locales gained a
  "timeout" entry, so a timeout-stopped run's history row is no
  longer blank either.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(i18n): stop the per-stage models card describing a deleted setting

The card said "a thorough run works in stages" and "fast runs use the active
model for everything and ignore this card" -- thorough/fast is the generation-
depth vocabulary deleted in the depth-collapse PR. There is no such choice any
more: tailoring against a job posting IS the staged run, unconditionally.

Not strictly false (a separate one-shot path still backs the résumé builder and
ai-generate), but it points at a setting the user no longer has. Reworded to
describe the two entry points by what they are -- with a job posting, or
without -- rather than by a removed setting name. Both locales.

The card itself stays: per-stage overrides are unrelated to the deleted agentic
system, and the seven rows match the current pipeline exactly (validate is
absent because it asks no model anything).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: scale the non-streaming completion deadline by effort too

analyze_job/match_evidence/strategy each make one non-streaming
Completer::complete_json round-trip, bounded by a FLAT 300s
(OLLAMA_COMPLETION) regardless of the run's chosen reasoning effort —
unlike the streamed draft/cover_letter calls, which already scale via
stream_deadline. A local model running at a HIGHER effort got no more
time on these three (first-running) stages than the baseline did, so
raising effort could not have saved a run that legitimately needed
longer on a slow local model.

- packages/shared/src/ai-timeouts.ts: new OLLAMA_COMPLETION_BASELINE_SECS
  + ollamaCompletionDeadlineSecs(effort), scaled by the SAME multiplier
  table stream_deadline uses. QUALITY_RUN_FIXED_SECS now covers only
  the repair fan-out + humanize (the two call sites with no effort to
  scale by, via Completer::complete); the three JSON stages moved to a
  new, effort-scaled QUALITY_RUN_JSON_STAGE_CALLS term in
  qualityRunDeadlineSecs. Regenerated via `pnpm gen:ipc`.
- timeouts.rs: OLLAMA_COMPLETION -> OLLAMA_COMPLETION_BASELINE (const)
  + ollama_completion_deadline(effort) (fn), mirroring stream_deadline.
  quality_run_deadline re-derived to match the TS formula exactly (both
  sides pin the same per-tier table).
- Completer::complete_json/structured_call/text_request now thread the
  run's effort through to the provider's StructuredCall, so
  ollama.rs's complete_impl can scale send_with_retry's deadline by it.
  complete/complete_with_usage (repair, humanize, chat_with_tools) keep
  the flat baseline unchanged — they take no AiGenerateRequest, so
  threading effort through them would ripple into every other caller
  of Completer::complete (autopilot notes, interview questions, the
  cover-letter fast path).
- Budget::RESUME_QUALITY.run_timeout (90 min) is UNCHANGED: it's the
  effort-blind floor, and multiplier is 1.0 there regardless of which
  term it applies to. Every tier above it grew to match the raised
  per-call ceiling on the JSON stages — doc comments across
  budget.rs/timeouts.rs/repair.rs updated to describe the new
  arithmetic rather than the old flat numbers.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): link a staged-pipeline generation to its application on save

persist_document built its AiGenerationRecord with ..empty_record(), whose
application_id is always None, and nothing else in the staged pipeline ever
set one -- merge_application only ever PRESERVES an existing link
(incoming.application_id.or(existing.application_id)), it never establishes
one. So the first staged-pipeline save for a posting with no prior linked
generation persisted application_id: NULL, invisible to every reader that
filters ai_generations by applicationId.

The résumé masked it: it has its own run-scoped read path
(PipelineRunDetail.resumeText, joined by run id, no link involved). The
cover letter has no such channel and was unreachable for that whole class
of application.

Mirrors the same idempotent ApplicationStore::upsert_for_origin call
ai_generations_save already makes, non-fatal on error like that path.

Also audited for other application_id-filtered ai_generations consumers this
silently broke: applications_delete's "delete everything" path
(AiGenerationStore::remove_for_application) never matched an orphaned row,
so deleting an application whose only linked document came from the staged
pipeline left that ai_generations row behind permanently -- not fixed here,
reported for a separate follow-up.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: include effort in the résumé stage cache key

Closes a stale-answer gap the previous commit opened: analyze_job/
match_evidence/strategy's Completer::complete_json now threads the
run's real effort to the provider (needed to scale the per-call
deadline), and on a thinking-capable Ollama model that reaches the
request as its own `think` field (ollama::think_level) -- which
changes the model's actual reasoning depth, not just how long the
caller waits. The stage cache key never carried effort, on the
(previously true) premise that it never reached the provider at all;
left alone, a "high"-effort answer could now be served back to a
"low"-effort request for the identical résumé/posting/model.

StageIdentity gains an `effort` field (mirroring context_window's
"reaches the request, so it's a key term" treatment); StageCacheKey
folds it into the pre-hash the same positional way. Investigated while
assessing FIX-3 (stage-artifact reuse on retry) -- the existing cache
IS the reuse mechanism the task asked about, and this closes the one
correctness gap that would have undermined trusting it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(applications): backfill the application link on orphaned generation rows

The FK fix in persist_document stops NEW rows being orphaned; it does
nothing for rows the staged pipeline already wrote before that fix
shipped, and applications_delete(keepDocuments=false) matches by
application_id -- an orphaned row is invisible to it. The user asks the
app to delete their documents and the documents stay: a privacy defect
on existing data, not a cosmetic gap.

link_orphaned_generations, run once per boot from ApplicationStore::open
(same guarded, non-fatal, cross-database posture as the existing
backfill_from_generations), links every ai_generations row with a
non-empty job_url and a NULL application_id to the Application that
already exists for its normalized job_url.

Deliberately lookup-only, never an upsert: unlike backfill_from_
generations (which predates ADR-0001 -- no Application ever existed for
those rows), a staged-pipeline run is always launched FROM an
Application's own page, so the Application for an orphaned row almost
always already exists. A row this cannot match means either the user
deleted that Application (creating one here would resurrect it) or the
row was never linked to begin with -- both must stay NULL. A wrong link
is worse than a missing one.

No schema migration: the application_id column and its index already
exist from AiGenerationStore's own add_application_id migration: this is
data repair, so there is nothing to append to either store's
position-indexed MIGRATIONS array.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test: prove a retry reuses the json stages that already succeeded

Closes the gap the FIX-3 investigation flagged: the reuse-on-retry
behaviour (analyze_job/match_evidence answer instantly from the stage
cache on a retry after strategy timed out, per the incident) was an
emergent property of independently-tested pieces -- key derivation,
KvCache read/write, per-stage hit/miss -- with nothing asserting the
scenario end to end. A future change to key derivation, the ledger, or
stage ordering could have broken it while every existing test stayed
green.

a_retry_after_a_mid_run_failure_does_not_re_spend_the_stages_that_already_succeeded
wires a real KvCache (tempdir) through the same StageCacheKey::new /
cache::get / cache::put sequence each real stage's run() performs
(cached_stage_call mirrors it verbatim, since this crate has no Tauri
test harness to construct a real Completer/AppHandle for the actual
stage structs). Asserts on a provider-call counter, not wall-clock or
a cached flag:

- first attempt: analyze_job + match_evidence succeed (1 call each),
  strategy fails (1 call, no cached answer to write);
- retry with unchanged inputs: analyze_job/match_evidence make ZERO
  further calls (a re-ask would panic inside the closure), strategy
  runs for real again since nothing cached it;
- a third attempt at a DIFFERENT effort must still miss analyze_job's
  cache -- the scenario where dropping `effort` back out of
  StageCacheKey (reverting the previous commit) shows up as a REAL
  re-spend of a stale-effort answer, not just a unit-level hash
  mismatch.

Mutation-tested by hand (applied and reverted, not assumed): forcing
cache::get to always return None reddens the retry section; dropping
`effort` from StageCacheKey::key's pre-hash reddens the third section
specifically.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor: extract the timeout/network transport-error mapping into one helper

Four provider adapters (anthropic/openai/gemini/ollama) duplicated the same
is_timeout()-to-AppError classification verbatim, pushing anthropic.rs over
the R8 hard LOC cap. map_completion_transport_error in ai_provider/mod.rs
now owns the mapping (and its is_timeout() rationale comment) once; each
adapter calls it with its own provider label and per-call deadline.

* test: pin the timeout/network transport-error classification

map_completion_transport_error had zero end-to-end coverage after the
duplication-removal refactor: a mutation test forcing it to always return
Network reddened nothing workspace-wide. Adds a test that drives it with a
real is_timeout()-producing local-socket timeout and a real refused
connection, asserting AppError::Timeout vs AppError::Network — the first
link in the is_timeout() -> Timeout -> StoppedReason::Timeout -> UI-banner
chain this batch's timeout reporting depends on.

* fix: make the ai_generations fk backfill link-first, never resurrect deletes

link_orphaned_generations (lookup-only) now runs before the wide,
create-capable backfill_from_generations on every ApplicationStore::open,
so a row it can resolve never reaches the wide backfill's clobbering merge
— the previous order made the lookup-only pass dead in production.

The wide backfill also gains a vintage gate (APPLICATIONS_FEATURE_EPOCH_MS,
a day before PR #359 merged): it may still create an Application for a
row provably predating the Applications feature, but a row at or after
that boundary is only ever linked, never created for. Without this, an
unconditional create-on-miss silently resurrected an Application the user
had just deleted (either delete arm) on the very next boot.

Adds a boot-path regression test (ApplicationStore::open itself, not the
private methods directly) plus three resurrection guards, each
mutation-tested by disabling the relevant gate and confirming it reddens.

* fix: refuse to save a résumé or letter that echoes a prompt-fence tag

save_verdict now checks contains_fence_tag on both the draft résumé and
the cover letter, in addition to the existing work-history-loss check —
draft and cover_letter are the sole producers of these documents (unlike
humanize/repair, which can discard a bad candidate and keep the last-good
text), so this is the last chokepoint before persistence that can catch a
leaked <generated_resume>/<candidate_resume> wrapper before it reaches the
saved aggregate and the exported PDF.

Refusing to save (fail-closed) rather than saving with a flagged report is
deliberate, matching the existing work-history refusal's precedent: a raw
framework artifact reaching an employer is worse than a document the user
has to retry. SaveVerdict::Refused now carries a user-facing reason so the
two defects don't share a misleading message.

* test: add a store-level guard for the ai_generations application_id fk

persist_document_establishes_the_application_fk_it_used_to_skip asserts on
persist_document's SOURCE TEXT — it would stay green even if
upsert_for_origin errored on every call, or try_state::<ApplicationStore>()
returned None at runtime, since neither shows up in the source.

persist_document itself still can't be driven directly (no tauri::test
mock-app harness), so the new test drives the STORE-LEVEL chain it
composes instead: upsert_for_origin's returned id lands on
AiGenerationRecord.application_id, save_application persists it, and
remove_for_application actually finds and deletes the row through it —
mutation-tested by forcing application_id: None, which reddens it.

The source pin stays (it still catches the call disappearing from
persist_document, which the store-level test structurally cannot).

* fix: guard the generating-panel elapsed anchor against 0 and clock skew

runStartedAt now falls back to null for a 0/negative startedAt, not just
null/undefined, so GeneratingPanel's own runStartedAt ?? mountFallback
recovers instead of anchoring the elapsed caption on the Unix epoch.
GeneratingPanel additionally clamps the tick at 0 so a startedAt that
passed the > 0 guard but is still ahead of this client's clock (skew)
can't render a negative "N total" caption.

Not reachable with today's now_ms()-populated pipeline_runs.started_at
column, so this is defensive; renderer-only, no frontend agent active.

* fix(pipeline): stop persist_document from resurrecting a deleted application

persist_document called ApplicationStore::upsert_for_origin, which creates
an Application unconditionally on a job_url miss. A staged run takes
minutes; if the user deletes the Application it was launched from while
the run is still working, the run landing and upserting on that job_url
silently resurrected the delete -- no race required, just the plain
sequence run-in-flight -> delete -> run lands.

Same hazard e695f4cf closed for ApplicationStore::link_orphaned_generations
at its own call site, three commits earlier in this batch -- that fix
never reached this call site. Switch to the same read-only primitive,
find_by_job_url: on a miss, leave application_id: None instead of creating
one. The normal case (Application still exists) is unaffected -- the FK
still gets set and the cover letter stays findable by Application-scoped
readers.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(ai-provider): pin the ollama completion baseline, not the stream one

Both cross-language tests asserted ollama_completion_deadline /
ollamaCompletionDeadlineSecs against STREAM_BASELINE_SECS /
stream_deadline, but the two baselines are documented as separate
constants free to drift independently — they only share a value today.
The old assertions would go red the moment someone made that sanctioned
change, misdirecting blame at the shared multiplier table. Assert
against OLLAMA_COMPLETION_BASELINE(_SECS) instead, with the multiplier
lookup reproduced inline so the check still catches real divergence in
the shared table rather than becoming a tautology.

* fix: gate the résumé pipeline save on ctx.letter, not letter_text()'s fallback

persist_document (and execute's own copy of the same decision) gated
save_verdict on ctx.letter_text(), which falls back to the user's own
pasted reference letter (input.cover_letter) whenever the cover_letter
stage produced nothing (include_cover_letter = false). That text is
never what cover_letter_text persists, so a registered fence tag
occurring incidentally inside a pasted letter (<question> is a
realistic one) refused the entire save - resume, report and all -
over a defect that could never reach the saved document.

Gate ctx.letter instead: the stage's own output, the only letter text
this run can actually persist. A leaked tag in the MODEL's own letter
output still refuses the save, since it lands in ctx.letter directly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: localize the résumé pipeline's per-call timeout banner

timeout_message spliced the raw internal stage key straight into an
un-translatable English sentence ("The \"match_evidence\" step didn't
get a response within 302s."), reaching job.failed's event data
verbatim after a run the user may have watched for minutes.

job_fail now has a job_fail_with_data sibling that carries structured
{ kind, stage, seconds } as the event payload instead of a
pre-formatted string; the resume pipeline's per-call-timeout arm is
the one caller that uses it (every other job_fail site is unchanged).
The renderer's useResumePipelineSession recognizes the shape and
renders it through the existing pipeline.timeout / pipeline.stage.*
i18n keys (en/de), falling back to the raw stage key for a build that
doesn't have a label for it yet. timeout_message's English fallback
still lands on the job's own tracked (un-localized) error field.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(ai-provider): correct the quality-run-deadline headroom claim

quality_run_deadline_clears_the_inner_per_call_bounds asserted >= against
a value that is provably identical at every effort tier, and its doc
comment borrowed research_deadline's "must clear with headroom" rule even
though RunDeadline is only ever polled between calls (never raced against
an in-flight completion the way research_deadline's tokio::time::timeout
wrap is), so no headroom is needed for the last inner call's own timeout
to win. Rename to quality_run_deadline_equals_the_inner_per_call_bounds,
assert_eq!, and document why exact equality is safe here.

* docs(ai-provider): correct is_timeout() classification claims

reqwest 0.13's Error::is_timeout() walks the whole error source chain
(its own TimedOut marker, hyper::Error::is_timeout(), a raw
io::ErrorKind::TimedOut) rather than narrowly matching only the
client's own .timeout() call. That's still the correct bucket here:
net::http::shared sets no separate connect/read timeout, so every
request's only timing bound is the same per-call .timeout() these
call sites set, and it covers connect through the last streamed
byte — but the comments overstated the mechanism as excluding
connect/DNS/TLS failures generally. Correct map_completion_transport_error's
doc and the assumption-pinning test's header comment; the URL/secret
scrubbing on the Network branch is untouched.

* test(ai-provider): make the refused-connection timeout tests race-safe

tests.rs and anthropic_tests.rs both bind an ephemeral loopback port,
close it, then unconditionally assert the next request is refused —
both compile into the same test binary and run in parallel by
default, so a sibling test can reclaim the freed port in between and
turn the connection into an accidental success or a slow response,
failing the test for a reason unrelated to is_timeout() classification.
Extract a refused_connection_error() helper per file that retries
against a fresh port (bounded, 5 attempts) instead of accepting
whatever the first attempt produces.

* fix: run the legacy generations backfill exactly once, ever

backfill_from_generations ran on every ApplicationStore::open and only
skipped a row once application_id was set or created_at crossed the
epoch guard. Deleting an Application detaches its generation rows back
to application_id=NULL without touching created_at, so a genuinely
pre-epoch row stayed pre-epoch and unlinked forever -- the next boot's
unconditional re-scan recreated the Application the user just deleted.
The epoch guard narrowed that window; it never closed it.

Add a durable backfill_state marker (new append-only migration) and
check it first: once the one-time legacy backfill has completed for a
data dir, later boots skip it entirely. link_orphaned_generations stays
safe to re-run every boot since it is lookup-only and can never create
an Application.

Split the backfill + its marker out of applications/mod.rs into
migrations.rs (same store, same pattern as reminders.rs/contact.rs) to
stay under the R8 LOC cap, and allowlist that file for R3's rusqlite
confinement rule, mirroring the existing per-domain-store entries.

* test(applications): close two mutation-surviving gaps in the backfill link tests

Every existing link_orphaned_generations test seeds the orphan row with
an already-normalized job_url, so deleting the internal
normalize_job_url call inside link_orphaned_generations still leaves
every one of them green. Add a test that seeds the RAW url a genuine
pre-fix row would carry.

Also add a test at exactly APPLICATIONS_FEATURE_EPOCH_MS: every
existing epoch-guard test uses a value safely past the boundary, so
`>` silently passes where `>=` is required. This pins the inclusive
boundary directly.

* fix: round a per-call timeout up to whole seconds, never truncate to 0s

timeout_message and timeout_failure_data both divided milliseconds by
1000, truncating down. A sub-second per-call timeout -- reachable once
effort scales the deadline down far enough -- rendered "within 0s" and
shipped seconds: 0 to the renderer's timeout banner.

Extract a shared round_up_seconds (div_ceil(1000).max(1)) so the
English message and the structured event payload always agree on the
same non-zero rounded value. Update the two pinned tests for the
rounding change (300_021ms now reports 301s, not 300s -- ceiling, not
truncation) and add a dedicated sub-second regression test where
truncation and ceiling diverge to 0 vs 1.

* fix: match the save verdict exhaustively instead of unreachable!()

The Ok(()) if refused arm re-derived the refusal reason by
re-destructuring verdict with a let-else unreachable!() fallback,
trusting it to stay in sync with the separately-computed refused bool.
A future edit to one without the other would panic inside the spawned
run task, leaving the job with no terminal event.

Nest a single exhaustive match on the verdict inside the Ok(()) arm
instead, so a new verdict variant is a compile error here, never a
runtime panic on a fallible path.

* fix(applications): correct the architecture-allowlist claim about the backfill's connection

The allowlist comment said applications/migrations.rs's persistence "lives
entirely inside the applications domain store, on the SAME connection" -
false: backfill_from_generations (and link_orphaned_generations) open a
second connection onto the sibling ai_generations.db to read and link its
rows. Reword to match the code.

* fix(applications): stop leaking a path through the boot-time backfill warn logs

Both open()-time warn! calls interpolated the AppError's Display directly.
rusqlite::Error::InvalidPath embeds the offending filesystem path in its
Display text, which AppError::from preserves, so a failed
crate::db::open(&gen_path) could log an absolute path (repo path-privacy
rule, and the same thing tests::architecture::r15_no_display_in_log_macros
already guards against generally). Log AppError::code() instead - a fixed,
path-free category string, exactly what it exists for.

* fix(applications): stop legacy_backfill_done swallowing a real read error into false

Every query_row error, not just QueryReturnedNoRows, was mapped to false via
is_ok() - a transient SQLite failure looked identical to "not done yet" and
re-ran the one-shot legacy scan, which recreates a deliberately-deleted
Application (the exact bug the marker exists to prevent), reachable through
a different door. Return AppResult<bool> and use .optional()? so only
QueryReturnedNoRows reads as "not done"; every other error now propagates
through backfill_from_generations's existing ? into ApplicationStore::
open's non-fatal warn-log path.

* fix(applications): log dropped legacy generation rows instead of silently discarding them

.filter_map(|r| r.ok()) discarded any row whose column mapping failed, then
the one-shot marker got set as if every row had been processed - so a
dropped row is never retried. Count the drops and log them at warn once the
scan finishes; the message is a bare count only, never the row's id/company/
url (path-free, content-free per ADR-027), since the marker this scan feeds
is one-shot and this is the only signal the loss is ever diagnosable from.

* fix(applications): relink stranded legacy generations after a restore, not just at boot

data_import replaces aiGenerations wholesale via AiGenerationStore::import,
but never touched the legacy-backfill marker. Restoring a pre-
ApplicationStore-era backup (one whose bundle has no "applications" section)
left its generations with application_id = NULL forever: the marker is
already set from the very first boot, long before any later restore, so
ApplicationStore::open's one-shot scan never even sees them again.

Extract the scan body into scan_legacy_generations (shared, marker-free) and
add ApplicationStore::relink_legacy_generations_after_restore, called from
data_import only when the bundle replaced aiGenerations but carries no
"applications" section - i.e. verifiably predates ApplicationStore, so none
of its rows can be a deliberately AiGenerationStore::detach_application-ed
row (that capability did not exist yet when such a bundle was exported).
A modern bundle that DOES carry "applications" is left alone: it already
restores self-consistent application_id links via the two imports, and CAN
legitimately carry a deliberately-detached row that re-scanning would
resurrect - the exact bug the one-shot marker exists to prevent.

* test(applications): cover the marker-set-last guarantee on a partial backfill failure

Only the success path was tested. Poison one row's link-back write with a
SQLite trigger so backfill_from_generations fails strictly between the
first row's committed Application and the second row's write, then assert
the one-shot marker stays unset and a later boot retries and finishes the
row it never reached, without spawning a duplicate Application for the row
whose creation already succeeded before its own write failed.

* fix(data): resolve the restore relink data dir like setup and test its gate

Two review findings on the restore-specific relink, both in one file.

The relink resolved its directory with a bare `app.path().app_data_dir()` and
skipped entirely when that failed. Setup resolves through
`resolve_and_export_data_dir`, which falls back to `platform::config::data_dir()`
— so on a host where the bare call errors, every store still opened through the
fallback and the one-shot boot marker got set, while the relink (the only thing
that can still repair those rows) silently did not run. The marker turns a
skipped repair into a permanent one, so the two resolutions must not differ.

The gate `aiGenerations present && applications absent` is the whole boundary
that stops a modern full backup from resurrecting a deliberately-detached row,
and nothing tested it. Lifted into a pure `is_legacy_generations_only_bundle`
and tested across all four combinations, exactly one of which may return true.
Chosen over a source-pin test: a pin asserts text exists in a file, not that
the decision is right, and goes stale silently when the code is reshaped.

Mutation-tested all three ways the condition can be weakened — `&&` to `||`,
and dropping either operand — each reddens the four-combination test.

head_commit.message:
feat: delete the agentic surfaces and extract the prompt fencing (#995)

* fix(renderer): close reset()'s stale-ref window in the resume pipeline session

reset() cleared runId/jobId/busy via setState but left runIdRef/jobIdRef/
busyRef stale until the next render body ran, mirroring the start() race
fixed in #993: a pipeline:stage or job.failed listener still mounted on the
just-reset run can fire in that gap and be misread as belonging to the next
session. Assign the three refs synchronously in reset(), same as start().

* refactor(agent): extract adr-010 prompt-fencing primitives into prompt_fence

PR-5 step 1 (drop agentic surfaces): pulls fenced/JOB_CAP/RESUME_CAP/
FENCE_TAG_PATTERNS/neutralize_transcript_boundaries out of agent::tools into a
new dependency-free crate::prompt_fence module so the pipeline, extension
bridge, and structured-output re-ask path keep their injection defense once
agent/ is deleted in step 2. AUTOPILOT_NOTE_SYSTEM moves into
autopilot_helpers, its only remaining consumer.

Pure move: every existing test travels with its primitive, unchanged, plus a
mutation check (verified, then reverted) confirming a broken fenced() still
fails pipeline::resume::test::every_untrusted_block_is_fenced_and_forgery_resistant.
ECHO_CAP/clamped_echo stay in agent::tools — no surviving consumer needs them.

tests/architecture.rs: classifies prompt_fence as L0, drops the now-dead
pipeline->agent and autopilot_helpers->agent R7 exceptions, and allowlists
prompt_fence->ipc_contracts for the generated RESUME_CAP constant (same shape
as the existing pipeline/ai_config/scraping exceptions).

* docs(architecture): sync layer doc with the prompt_fence extraction

Mirrors the tests/architecture.rs change from the previous commit: adds
prompt_fence to the L0 list, replaces the resolved autopilot_helpers->agent
TODO(arch) note with what actually happened, and folds the new
prompt_fence->ipc_contracts exception into the R7 table row.

* refactor(agent): delete the agentic backend (prep-application + confirm gate)

PR-5 step 2: removes agent/ in its entirety (controller, flows, gate, tools,
tools_pipeline, tools_quality) plus commands/agent.rs (the agent_run/
agent_confirm Tauri commands), their lib.rs/commands/mod.rs registrations,
the AgentGate managed state, and Budget::{AGENT_PREP, AGENT_IMPROVE} +
their compile-time relations and tests in pipeline/budget.rs. Everything
this programme's step 1 extracted into prompt_fence and autopilot_helpers
survives untouched.

Kept deliberately (verified against the still-untouched renderer, PR-5 step
3): ipc_contracts::agent (AgentRunRequest/AgentConfirmRequest) and
agent_flow_kinds (AGENT_FLOW_KINDS), the tauri-client agent namespace, and
the packages/shared schemas backing them — removing any of these breaks
`pnpm typecheck` on renderer code this PR does not touch.
limits::AGENT_RUN_* stay too: commands/resume_pipeline's admission control
(the staged pipeline's cancel registration) uses them, confirmed by grep, not
assumption. commands::resume_pipeline::resume_pipeline_run is now the third
CancelRegistry registrant in place of the deleted agent_run.

Transitive orphans found by the delete-and-cargo-check method (not by
reading the call graph) and removed: resume_pipeline::sync_saved_resume_status
(agent::tools::save_resume_handler was its only caller) and
Completer::capabilities (only agent::controller ever called it — the
provider tool-calling surface it fed, AiProvider::chat_with_tools/ToolSpec/
AgentTurn across every provider adapter, is now unreachable too, but lives
in the ai-provider domain excluded from this author's paths; flagged for
that domain's owner rather than deleted here).

Every surviving file's doc comments that named agent/agent::* code are
rewritten to say so honestly (past tense, "now-deleted") rather than left
pointing at nothing — verified with a targeted grep sweep, not assumed
clean. tests/architecture.rs drops agent's L3 classification; its own test
suite (18 tests) still passes, confirming the layer model stays internally
consistent.

* fix(match-resume): drop jobpostingmeta's write-only location field

Unrelated to the agent deletion — found because it turns cargo clippy
-D warnings red (dead_code), one of this task's gates. Verified via git
history that the deleted agent/tools.rs never read it either, so this
was already dead before PR-5 started, not a fallout of this change.

* test(extension): close the answer-assist forgery-defense coverage gap

Found while proving prompt_fence's extraction is safe for PR-5 step 2:
every existing answer_assist/answer_rewrite test covers the LEGITIMATE-input
shape of build_user_message/build_rewrite_user_message (the right tags
appear), but none feeds either function a hostile payload — disabling
crate::prompt_fence::fenced's neutralization pass left all 53 existing
tests in this module green.

Adds one hostile-input regression test per call site (mirrors the pattern
already used in prompt_fence::test and pipeline::resume::test), each
mutation-verified: disabling neutralization turns the new test red while
every other test in the module stays green.

* chore(ipc): keep agent_flow_kinds' generated doc accurate

The doc comment gen-ipc-rust.ts emits for AGENT_FLOW_KINDS named the
agent::flows registry this Rust test used to pin — deleted in the previous
commit. Updates the generator's template (not the generated file directly,
which is DO-NOT-EDIT-BY-HAND) and regenerates via `pnpm gen:ipc`.

* docs(architecture): drop agent from the l3 layer doc

Mirrors the tests/architecture.rs change from the agent-deletion commit:
removes agent from the L3 module list (both the layer table and the
per-layer section header) and updates the prompt_fence exception note now
that agent no longer exists to reach.

* refactor(renderer): drop the agent-run flow's renderer surfaces

Removes PrepApplicationPanel, AgentConfirm, ImproveResumeRun,
useAgentRunSession, the use-agent service hooks, and the
agent-run.machine state machine -- the last renderer consumers of
agent.run/confirm/onStep. The prep_application and improve_resume
flows are dropped per owner decision; the extension's answer-assist
is unaffected (separate backend + extension surface).

The tauri-client agent namespace and ipc_contracts::agent stay for
now -- a later step removes those once nothing in the renderer calls
them.

* refactor(renderer): drop the tailored-résumé panel and its wiring

TailoredResumePanel's only remaining reason to exist was hosting the
now-deleted ImproveResumeRun review; its OTHER capability (the staged
résumé pipeline: quality report, fabrication review, per-section fix,
run history) is fully duplicated by TailorFlow's own ResultsPanel, so
nothing it hosted goes unreachable. JobDetailPane's trigger button is
removed too -- the existing one-shot "Tailor" button (handleTailor)
stays as this posting's tailor affordance.

stopped-reason.ts's doc comment is updated: the agent-run consumer of
its map is gone, leaving only the staged pipeline's pipeline.stopped.*
labels.

* chore(translations): prune jobs.tailored / jobs.prep keys, en + de

Orphaned by the agentic-surface and TailoredResumePanel deletions --
nothing renders these strings any more. Key parity between en and de
verified after the cut.

* refactor(ipc): delete the agent wire contract end to end

PR-5 step 4 (final): with the renderer's agentic surfaces gone (step 3), the
tauri-client callers of api.agent.run/confirm/onStep that forced this
contract to stay are gone too, so the whole wire contract goes with them —
schema, generated Rust, TS client, and every layer between.

Deletes: AGENT_FLOW_KINDS/AgentRunRequestSchema/AgentConfirmRequestSchema
and their inferred types (packages/shared/src/schemas/index.ts);
ipc/contracts/agent.ts (AgentContract, AgentStepEvent, AGENT_CHANNELS) and
its wiring in ipc/contracts/index.ts; events/agent.ts (AGENT_EVENTS) and its
wiring in events/index.ts; the tauri-client agent namespace and its
registration in tauri-client/index.ts; ipc_contracts::agent and
ipc_contracts::agent_flow_kinds on the Rust side, regenerated away (not
hand-deleted) by fixing gen-ipc-rust.ts's template and running `pnpm
gen:ipc` — caught by gen:ipc:check once already this PR, so this time the
generator changed first.

Kept and verified, not assumed: agent-caps.ts and the generated
ipc_contracts::agent_caps::AGENT_RESUME_TEXT_CAP it backs are untouched —
confirmed byte-identical after regeneration (git status shows no diff on
agent_caps.rs) — because prompt_fence::RESUME_CAP depends on that path and
prompt_fence is what keeps the résumé pipeline and the extension's
answer-assist fenced. limits::AGENT_RUN_* stay too, per the prior step's
confirmed admission-control use in commands/resume_pipeline.

Transitive orphans found and fixed (delete-and-compile, not call-graph
reading): pipeline::budget::test's AgentRunRequest security-lock test (its
subject is gone; the equivalent guard for the one remaining paying flow
already exists at commands::resume_pipeline::test::
run_request_carries_only_identity_no_budget_and_no_routing, so nothing is
newly uncovered) and the renderer's mock-client.ts, whose AppClient literal
carried an agent field TypeScript now rejects as excess — both found by
running the exact gates, not by reading the call graph.

* test(prompt-fence): make every fence_tag_patterns entry load-bearing

Security review: removing each of the 24 registry entries individually and
re-running the whole suite found 15 removable with everything green — 10 of
those are tags surviving code still emits. Only 9 entries were guarded by
anything. The gap: every_untrusted_block_is_fenced_and_forgery_resistant
does assert </job_analysis> appears once, but its hostile payload only ever
forges </job_posting>, so every entry that payload never mentions is inert
to that assertion no matter how many real tags surround it.

Adds one table-driven test looping an independent copy of the tag
vocabulary (deliberately NOT FENCE_TAG_PATTERNS.keys() — a first draft using
the live map silently stopped testing whatever was deleted from it, since
the deleted entry's own iteration disappears too). A set-equality check
against the live registry catches drift in both directions: a tag removed
from the registry is still asserted against by the hardcoded list (and
fails for real), and a tag added to the registry without a matching
addition to the list fails the equality check immediately.

Mutation-checked the way the review proved the gap: temporarily deleting
"web_search_notes" and, separately, "section_note" (two of the ten
previously-unguarded tags) from the registry literal, and verifying the
per-tag loop alone (equality check disabled) also independently catches a
removal — both verified by hand, then reverted before landing.

* test(extension): extend answer-assist fence coverage to all six blocks

answer_assist.rs::build_user_message fences six untrusted blocks; the
regression test only forged into question. The two with the strongest
attacker story were untested: company_research (a web-sourced brief) and
web_search_notes (search results) — fully attacker-influenced content, and
both among the previously-unguarded prompt_fence registry entries.
Behaviour was already correct; this closes the coverage gap so a future
regression in any one of the six is caught at its own call site rather than
inferred from question's.

Loops the same hostile payload (a forged <job_posting> sibling plus a
forged [tool_result:save_resume] marker) through each of the six slots in
turn, leaving the rest empty/absent so exactly one block is under test each
time. Mutation-checked: disabling fenced's neutralization pass turns this
red on the first case while the rest of the module's tests stay green.

* refactor: delete three more agent-era orphans the sweep missed

Found by the architect making every module private and diffing the
compiler's unused-item list against the same run at base — catches a pub
fn's dead_code lint exemption that delete-and-check-one-at-a-time relies on
the item already being pub(crate)/private to trip.

- commands/resume_pipeline/report.rs: for_saved_resume and
  agent_save_pipeline. Their only production caller was the deleted
  agent/tools.rs:843 (save_resume_handler). Two now-unused imports
  (crate::error::AppResult, crate::pipeline::resume::stages::validate_documents)
  go with them; the stale doc reference to a test that no longer exists
  (the_saved_resume_label_round_trips_through_the_shared_vocabulary, which
  lived in the deleted agent/tools/test.rs) goes with the function it
  described.
- pipeline/runs/mod.rs: PipelineRunStore::update_status_if_present. Its sole
  caller was the sync_saved_resume_status this PR already deleted; its only
  remaining references were its own test
  (a_status_move_never_resurrects_a_deleted_run in pipeline/runs/test.rs,
  removed alongside it), which is exactly why delete-and-compile missed it —
  a function whose only caller is its own test compiles clean forever.

Verified no further hidden orphans in either touched file: every remaining
pub fn in both has a real, traced production caller.

* refactor(prompt-fence): make resume_cap a genuine local literal

Both reviewers converged here. RESUME_CAP was imported from the generated
ipc_contracts::agent_caps::AGENT_RESUME_TEXT_CAP, which forced an
R7_ALLOW exception spanning L0->L3 — and that constant had no TS consumer
left after PR-5 step 3 deleted the renderer's improve_resume entry point
(its only reader), only the generator. JOB_CAP's own doc already states
the rule for this exact case: "A local literal — nothing outside this
crate reads it, and generating a number with one consumer is ceremony."

Deletes the generator target (genAgentCaps in gen-ipc-rust.ts, its
AGENT_RESUME_TEXT_CAP import, its outputs entry), the generated
ipc_contracts/agent_caps.rs, packages/shared/src/agent-caps.ts and its
barrel export, and the ("prompt_fence", "ipc_contracts") R7_ALLOW entry —
prompt_fence is dependency-free for real now, not by exception.

Value verified unchanged: 8_000 before and after. Mutation-checked:
temporarily setting the literal to 100 reddens
build_user_message_neutralizes_a_forged_boundary_in_every_untrusted_block
(the cap truncates the hostile payload before neutralization can reach the
marker's tail) — proof the tests still exercise the real value, not
something cached. r7_allowlist_has_no_dead_entries and
r7_no_upward_layer_imports both still pass with the entry gone.

* test(resume-pipeline): guard the error-echo clamp resolve.rs kept

resolve.rs::echoed clamps a request-supplied id to 64 chars before it is
echoed into a validation-error message — reimplemented locally because
agent::tools::ECHO_CAP/clamped_echo, the equivalent it mirrors, were never
part of the prompt_fence extraction. At base the rule was mutation-checked
by commands/agent.rs, which PR-5 deletes; nothing re-proved the clamp
survived on its new sole owner, so replacing echoed's body with
id.to_string() (no clamp at all) left the whole suite green.

Impact was already bounded — JOB_IDENTITY_CAP caps resumeId/jobId at 512
bytes before either ever reaches echoed — but a clamp guarded by nothing is
one refactor away from silently doing nothing. Adds one test per call site
(resolve_resume's "resume not found" / resolve_job's "job not found in
cache" errors), each with a 100-char id, asserting the message carries
exactly the first 64 chars and no more. Mutation-checked: dropping the
.take(...) from echoed's body reddens both.

* docs: repoint agent_run bucket + chat_with_tools comments at pr-5

limits/mod.rs's AGENT_RUN_RATE_MAX/CONCURRENCY_MAX/QUEUE_MAX docs still
described the bucket as the deleted agent_run command's; its sole caller
is now resume_pipeline_run. Reword to say so, and note the ceiling was
inherited rather than freshly reviewed for its new caller. Constants keep
their agent_run-derived names on purpose (rename is a separate call).

spend/mod.rs's chokepoint list still cited chat_with_tools as agent_run's
per-turn billing hook. agent_run is gone; chat_with_tools has no live
caller now. Flagged inline for the AI-provider owner as a follow-up, not
touched here — ToolSpec/AgentTurn dead-code status is theirs to act on.

* docs(knowledge): drop the agent module from the knowledge base

domain-model.md still documented the flow registry, the wire vocabulary, both
flows, their budgets, the tool-call ceiling and gated saves via
report::for_saved_resume -- all deleted in this PR. architecture.md still listed
agent/ and commands/agent.rs under Automation and in the feature-ownership
table.

Left standing deliberately: prompt_fence is now an L0 security primitive owning
ADR-010 fencing, and BOTH the staged résumé pipeline and the extension's
answer-assist depend on it. The extension's AI drafting survived this deletion
on purpose -- a reader who sees 'the agent was deleted' could reasonably
conclude otherwise.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: close the self-closing tag gap in the fence-tag pattern

compile_fence_tag_pattern required whitespace before any trailing
content after a tag name, so a self-closer with no leading space
(<job_posting/>) rode through fenced() byte-identical, attributes and
all. The group now opens on whitespace OR a slash, then reads to the
next '>' the same way the attribute form always did, which also closes
duplicated-slash and slash-then-attribute variants the reviewer's own
suggested pattern would still have missed.

Extends the registry-wide regression test to probe every registered
tag with a self-closing and a plain-opening forgery, not just the one
tag the earlier example covered.

* docs: drop dangling intra-doc links to the deleted agent budgets

Budget::AGENT_PREP/AGENT_IMPROVE were deleted with the agent module,
but the module doc still used rustdoc link syntax for them; cargo
doc's broken_intra_doc_links (warn-by-default) flags both. Switched
to plain backticks, matching the same names' own convention lower in
the same file. Swept the crate for other dangling links to deleted
agent items; none found outside this file.

Also drives every_shipped_budget_is_internally_consistent from a
const slice of shipped budgets instead of reading RESUME_QUALITY
directly, so a future second budget (already anticipated in this
file's own doc) is covered by construction instead of the test
silently keeping green while checking nothing new.

* docs: correct the skills_present/absent truncation rationale

The comment described "the consumer" truncating skills_present/
skills_absent into a prompt as an ongoing fact, but its only named
example is explicitly the now-deleted agent::tools_quality module and
the crate's sole current caller (pipeline::resume::stages::strategy)
reads only .roles from extract_evidence. Reworded to state the
ordering is sized for a future truncating consumer rather than
implying a live one; sort behavior unchanged.

* test(renderer): make the reset() stale-ref test actually fail without the fix

The race test invoked the pipeline:stage listener via optional chaining, so
a missing registration would silently no-op instead of failing the test.
Assert both listeners are registered before firing them, exercise jobIdRef
and busyRef (not just runIdRef) with a synchronous stale job.failed, and
reword the comment to describe reset()'s synchronous ref guard rather than
the pre-fix behavior it replaced.

---------

content after a tag name, so a self-closer with no leading space

silently keeping green while checking nothing new.

skills_absent into a prompt as an ongoing fact, but its only named
example is explicitly the now-deleted agent::tools_quality module and
the crate's sole current caller (pipeline::resume::stages::strategy)

ordering is sized for a future truncating consumer rather than
implying a live one; sort behavior unchanged.

a missing registration would silently no-op instead of failing the test.

autopilot_helpers, its only remaining consumer.

mutation check (verified, then reverted) confirming a broken fenced() still
fails pipeline::resume::test::every_untrusted_block_is_fenced_and_forgery_resistant.
ECHO_CAP/clamped_echo stay in agent::tools — no surviving consumer needs them.

prompt_fence to the L0 list, replaces the resolved autopilot_helpers->agent

prompt_fence->ipc_contracts exception into the R7 table row.

tools_pipeline, tools_quality) plus commands/agent.rs (the agent_run/
agent_confirm Tauri commands), their lib.rs/commands/mod.rs registrations,
the AgentGate managed state, and Budget::{AGENT_PREP, AGENT_IMPROVE} +
their compile-time relations and tests in pipeline/budget.rs. Everything
this programme's step 1 extracted into prompt_fence and autopilot_helpers
survives untouched.

assumption. commands::resume_pipeline::resume_pipeline_run is now the third

head_commit.message:
build: pin the rust toolchain across local, ci, and release (#994)

* build: pin rust toolchain to 1.96.1 across local, ci, and release

Local dev, PR CI, and release builds each resolved whatever "stable" meant
on the day, so they could silently disagree (a bare cargo fmt --all mass-
reformatted files that pass cargo fmt --check under the pinned rustfmt).

Add apps/desktop/src-tauri/rust-toolchain.toml pinning channel 1.96.1 (the
already-installed toolchain, frozen in place — not an upgrade) plus the
rustfmt/clippy/llvm-tools-preview components every gate needs. Add
rust-version = "1.95" to Cargo.toml, the real MSRV floor re-derived from
`cargo metadata`'s per-package rust_version fields (sysinfo 0.39.6 is the
highest at 1.95; serial_test 4.0.1 is next at 1.93.1).

dtolnay/rust-toolchain doesn't read toolchain files -- its @rev IS the
version selector -- so .github/actions/setup-rust (consumed by ci-pipeline,
quality, and security workflows) and release.yml's inline setup step both
move from the @stable branch to the repo's own "1.96.1" branch SHA.

Verified locally: rustup auto-installs and activates 1.96.1 with the pinned
components via the toolchain-file override, and cargo fmt --check/test/
clippy and pnpm typecheck all pass under it -- no reformat commit needed.

* fix: correct the rust pin to 1.97.1 and drop unused components

workflow_runs.display_title: feat(pipeline): delete the max generation depth and the depth concept…

head_commit.message:
feat(pipeline): delete the max generation depth and the depth concept (#993)

* fix(ai-generate): drop the dead depth picker from the fine-tune wizard step

The staged-depth control in StepFineTune wrote aiGenerate.depth but nothing
ever read it back — the wizard's Generate button always ran the fast
one-shot path regardless of the picker, so the affordance was decorative.
Removes the control plus its now-orphaned session-store field and i18n key.

TailoredResumePanel and its depth-selection UI stay for now: it also hosts
the agentic "Improve this résumé" review (#986), which #992 never ported to
the apply flow's ResultsPanel — deleting it here would silently drop a
recently-shipped feature. See .claude/scratch/drop-generation-depths.md.

* feat(jobs): delete the depth-selection ui, keep the tailored-résumé panel as the improve host

Removes DepthSelector, SectionTimeline, GenerationDepthPreferences, and
lib/generate/generation-depth.ts now that the apply flow runs the staged
pipeline unconditionally (#992) and every generate/tailor surface stopped
offering a depth choice. Strips the depth picker and section timeline out
of the tailored-résumé panel rather than deleting it outright — it still
hosts the agentic "Improve this résumé" review (#986), which a follow-up
PR deletes alongside its own agent-run plumbing; deleting the panel here
would have orphaned that flow for one PR. Every staged run from this panel
is now a hardcoded quality-depth run.

Drops the pipeline machine's per-section fold (foldSectionStates and the
sectionStates it fed) since SectionTimeline was its only consumer, and the
generationDepth field from the preferences store/schema. Pins the historic
depth-label vocabulary in PipelineRunsList (old run rows still need to
render fast/quality/max) and adds an orphan-key rehydrate test for the
now-removed preferences field — both mutation-tested.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(pipeline): delete the max generation depth and the llm judge

The max depth wasted tokens for no acted-on value (12+ calls a run,
and llm_judge's Warning-only opinions nothing consumed) — PR-4 step 2
removes the Rust half: max_pipeline/MAX_STAGES, the section-generation
stage and its typed answers, the judge stage, GenerationDepth and the
run request's depth field, the max-only budget/deadline constants
(both sides), and the section-wise progress observer. The staged
pipeline is quality-only now.

RunRow.depth keeps its column (writes "quality" on every new run; an
existing fast/quality/max row still reads back with no migration).
GENERATION_DEPTHS stays in packages/shared as a read-only historic
vocabulary — the renderer still needs it to parse an old max-depth
report without relabelling it. reseed_projects (max-only, unreferenced
once section_gen.rs is gone) is also removed.

* fix(renderer): drop the deleted depth field and pipeline stages from call sites

Mechanical fallout of the shared depth-field/PIPELINE_STAGES removal:
TailoredResumePanel stops sending depth (the request has no field to
carry it now), resume-pipeline.machine and the apply-flow checklist no
longer fold sections/assemble/llm_judge, and ModelAdvisor's per-stage
context-fit table drops its two max-only entries — the worst-case
stage is strategy now, not sections. Includes the matching test/fixture
updates and a new regression test pinning that a historic max-depth
quality report still parses as max rather than degrading to fast.

* chore(i18n): remove translation keys for the deleted pipeline stages

sections/llm_judge (settings.ai.stages.names/descriptions) and
sections/assemble/llm_judge (pipeline.stage) no longer name a stage
this build runs — the max generation depth that produced them is gone.
en and de stay symmetric.

* refactor(pipeline): delete named_entry_range, entry_range, and identity_line

Their only callers were the deleted max-depth regenerate path and the
deleted pipeline/resume/max_test.rs — none of the three ever had a
real caller left after PR #990's depth removal, but pub-in-pub-mod
visibility meant dead_code could never flag them. Cascading private
helpers (entry_range_and_identity, EntryIdentity, same, DATE_COLUMN_GAP)
go with them. Rewrites the doc comments that named the deleted symbols.

* test(pipeline): pin the project separator glyph in the normalizer test

render_project's PROJECT_SEPARATOR had no literal assertion left after
max_test.rs was deleted — stubbing render_project still reddens 7
tests, but the exact glyph was free to drift silently on the owner's
showcase Projects section. Mutation-tested: flipping the separator to
" - " reddens this assertion; reverted after confirming.

* docs(ipc): drop the deleted generation depth from the pipeline contract

The contract doc still described a `quality`/`max` depth choice and
listed "a rejected depth" as a job.failed-before-the-run-row cause;
execute() no longer validates or rejects a depth at all.

* fix(i18n): restore historic pipeline.stage keys, drop the dead depth constant

frontend-reviewer HIGH: commit a15aa789 removed pipeline.stage.sections/
.assemble/.llm_judge from both locales, but PipelineRunsList still renders
those exact names off PERSISTED pipeline_run_events rows (a max run's
stored trail, reachable from both TailoredResumePanel and TailorFlow's
ResultsPanel) — no migration touches old rows, so a German user was seeing
raw English wire tokens next to translated ones. Restores all three keys
in both locales with the original copy, and adds a render-based test
against a persisted max-depth trail (not a key-existence check) so a
future cleanup pass that reintroduces this has to break an actual
assertion. Mutation-tested: deleting one restored key reddens both the new
render test and the i18n parity test.

Same reasoning, applied further: use-resume-pipeline-session's reconnect
replay sets the live stage label straight from the last PERSISTED event
regardless of whether the coarse machine still maps it, so TailoredResumePanel
and useTailorPipeline's stage captions were exposed to the identical gap —
fixed by the same three restored keys, since all three read sites share
the `pipeline.stage.*` namespace.

Also, per frontend-reviewer MEDIUM findings:
- Drops PIPELINE_RUN_DEPTHS_HISTORIC — it had zero production consumers
  (the component always interpolated generationDepth.option.*.label
  directly) and its own test's `toContain` assertion only proved the
  constant equals itself. The it.each label table — genuinely mutation-
  tested — is the real guard and stays.
- Sweeps the orphaned pipeline.section.* subtree (~17 keys x 2 locales):
  SectionTimeline was its only consumer and it's deleted. Verified first —
  the "Section verdicts" panel (SectionVerdicts/buildSectionVerdicts) uses
  the unrelated quality.panel.sections.* namespace and labels sections from
  the document's own heading text, never from these keys.

Enumerated every other persisted column this PR's deletions touch:
depth (PipelineRunSummary/Detail) — already guarded, confirmed real.
ai_stage_overrides per-stage rows — safe: the Rust command filters out
overrides for retired stages server-side, and resolveStageRouting only
ever iterates the current OVERRIDABLE_PIPELINE_STAGES list, so a stray
`sections`/`llm_judge` override key can never reach settings.ai.stages.*.
report.pipeline (QualityReport wrapper) — has no label render path at all.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(pipeline): amend adr-032 for the depth collapse and sweep stale comments

The staged résumé pipeline is now the only one: analyze_job → match_evidence
→ strategy → draft → cover_letter → validate → repair → humanize. ADR-032 is
amended to record why the depths collapsed — a Warning-only model opinion that
nothing acts on is pure token spend — and why the historic vocabulary
(GENERATION_DEPTHS, pipeline.stage.*) deliberately outlives the feature that
wrote it, so existing run rows still parse and render.

Also sweeps present-tense doc comments in surviving source that still described
deleted machinery (the max section fan-out, the judge, section_prompts), and
records the section-regeneration degrade: on a historic max run, regenerating
one role now rewrites the whole Work Experience section, because the per-entry
path went with max. That is the documented fallback, not a new defect, but it
is user-visible and belongs in the release notes.

Comments only in Rust — no behavior change. A first pass removed three entries
from FENCE_TAG_PATTERNS along with their comment; that is ADR-010 injection
fencing and a security call, not a docs call, so it was reverted and only the
comment rewritten.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): reconcile a job.failed that races ahead of resume-pipeline start()

resume_pipeline_run spawns its task and returns the ids immediately, so an
admission/validation failure can call job_fail before start()'s mutateAsync
even resolves — jobIdRef is still null/stale, so the live job.failed
listener drops the event, and (with no pipeline_runs row ever written
either) the session was left spinning in `starting` forever. start() now
reconciles once, right after the ids land, against the cheap in-memory
JobTracker read fetchJob already provides elsewhere for this exact class
of race.

* test(settings): pin what the search-index deletion actually removed

A bare length assertion passes even if the wrong entry were dropped, or a
duplicate masked a real removal. Assert the change directly instead:
ai-depth is gone, and ai-stages no longer carries the judge/sections
keywords that went with it. Mutation-tested by restoring both keywords —
the new assertion goes red.

* refactor(pipeline): correct stale repair-is-last-stage deadline comment

humanize now runs after repair (PR #991), so the deadline comment's claim
that repair has no boundary after it was wrong; describe repair's own
between-call check instead.

* refactor(pipeline): fix backwards free-stage deadline rationale

The Stage::costs_a_provider_call doc argued aborting at a free-stage
boundary conserves already-paid work; apply_stop does the opposite (it lets
a free stage run past the deadline). Reword to match: NOT aborting at a
free-stage boundary is what conserves the work already paid for.

* refactor(pipeline): rename types_max/assemble to project_seed/project_render

Both modules lost their max-depth contents when that generation depth was
removed; only ProjectOut and render_project (PR #990's deterministic
Projects normalization) survive. Rename the files to name what they
actually hold and trim the apologetic why-the-filename-is-wrong headers
down to their actual contract; that history belongs in the ADR.

* fix(shared): reword generation depths as legacy read-side vocabulary

resumePipeline.run's wire request has no depth field and every new run
persists "quality"; the doc comments still described the constant as if a
run could request a depth. Reword both the TS source and the Rust
generator (regenerated output included) to state new-run "quality" is
fixed and fast/quality/max exist only to read historic rows.

* docs(adr-032): separate the base provider-call count from the optional ones

The amendment said "4 LLM calls ... draft + letter", which does not say
which passes are counted. Honest cost is the point of this programme, so the
breakdown is now explicit: 4 base calls (analyze, evidence, strategy, draft),
then cover_letter only when includeCoverLetter is set (it defaults to false),
repair only when there are Criticals to fix, and humanize 0-2 -- it is
deterministic-first, so a draft with no voice flags costs nothing at all.

Each claim verified against the stage sources rather than restated.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): close the render-commit window left in the job.failed reconcile

jobIdRef/runIdRef/busyRef are all written in the hook's render body, so a
setState only reaches them once React actually re-renders — not
synchronously, and not necessarily before start()'s own next await resumes
(a promise resolved entirely through the microtask queue never yields the
macrotask turn React's scheduler needs). CodeRabbit found the residual
window this left in the previous reconcile fix: job.failed could arrive
right after the reconcile read came back clean but before that commit,
and still get dropped. Empirically, busyRef has the exact same property
(confirmed by a failing test before this fix), not just jobIdRef/runIdRef.

start() now assigns all three refs synchronously the instant each becomes
knowable — busy right after send('START') (which always lands on a busy
state), the ids right after they're returned — independent of when React
gets around to committing.

* docs(adr-032): stop calling the live routes depths

"Quality depth" and "Fast depth" were the vocabulary this PR removes: depth
is no longer a per-run setting anyone can choose. They are now the quality
pipeline (the staged run, the apply flow's only route) and the fast path (the
one-shot generation behind the résumé builder and ai-generate, for generating
without a job posting) -- a different job, not a cheaper setting on the same
one.

"Depth" now appears only where it is still true: the persisted read-side
vocabulary that keeps historic run rows rendering.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(adr-032): point the restated call limits at their owning symbols

The amendment quotes real numbers (the cover-letter default, the repair round
cap, the humanize bounds), so it has to say what owns them, or it silently
asserts a stale figure the first time someone retunes one.

Anchored to the symbols rather than to line numbers -- a line number rots
faster than the value it annotates, and points at nothing once the file moves.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
